pinyin: wài sheng dǎ dēng long —— zhào jiù
literal: nephew carrying a lantern: lighting up uncle (照舅)
meaning: same as before (照舅 puns on 照旧 'as usual')
origin: Traditional two-part allegorical saying; the second half is often left unsaid.

pinyin: kǒng fū zǐ bān jiā —— jìng shì shū
literal: Confucius moving house: nothing but books (书)
meaning: always losing (书 shū puns on 输 'to lose')
origin: Traditional xiehouyu; common among card and mahjong players.

pinyin: hé shang dǎ sǎn —— wú fǎ wú tiān
literal: a monk under an umbrella: no hair, no sky (无发无天)
meaning: lawless, defying all rules (无法 puns on 无发)
origin: Traditional xiehouyu; Mao Zedong famously applied it to himself.

term: 哑巴吃黄连——有苦说不出
pinyin: yǎ ba chī huáng lián —— yǒu kǔ shuō bù chū
literal: a mute eating bitter herb: bitterness he cannot voice
meaning: suffering in silence; unable to complain
origin: Traditional xiehouyu (黄连 = goldthread, extremely bitter).

pinyin: zhú lán dǎ shuǐ —— yī chǎng kōng
literal: fetching water with a bamboo basket: all for nothing

pinyin: xiǎo cōng bàn dòu fu —— yī qīng èr bái
literal: scallion with tofu: one green, one white

term: 猪八戒照镜子——里外不是人
pinyin: zhū bā jiè zhào jìng zi —— lǐ wài bú shì rén
literal: Pigsy looking in a mirror: not human inside or out
meaning: blamed by both sides; can't win
origin: From Journey to the West's pig-demon Zhu Bajie.

equivalent.en: damned if you do, damned if you don't

term: 黄鼠狼给鸡拜年——没安好心
pinyin: huáng shǔ láng gěi jī bài nián —— méi ān hǎo xīn
literal: the weasel paying New Year respects to the hen: up to no good
meaning: a friendly gesture hiding bad intentions

equivalent.es: cuando la limosna es grande, hasta el santo desconfía

pinyin: ní pú sà guò jiāng —— zì shēn nán bǎo
literal: a clay Buddha crossing a river: can't even save itself
meaning: too troubled yourself to help others

equivalent.en: I can barely keep my own head above water

pinyin: zhàng èr hé shang —— mō bù zháo tóu nǎo
literal: a ten-foot-tall monk: you can't reach his head

equivalent.en: I can't make heads or tails of it

pinyin: sī mǎ zhāo zhī xīn —— lù rén jiē zhī
literal: Sima Zhao's intentions: every passer-by knows them
origin: Three Kingdoms period: Emperor Cao Mao said this of the ambitious regent Sima Zhao.
